title: Naming, Column Pages, Fitting, Spying & Functions
description: Five jobs the browser just took off your hands — element naming, wrapped columns, text fitting, scrollspy and design tokens.

drops.title: Match Element
drops.description: A deck and a rail that reorder, filter and morph from one declaration instead of a unique name minted per row.
drops.concept: A view transition can only morph elements it can identify, and view-transition-name has to be globally unique — which meant generating an id per list item in JavaScript. match-element lets the browser derive identity from the element itself, so a whole collection becomes animatable with one rule, while view-transition-class tunes every group at once and transition types give reorder and filter their own choreography.
drops.source: Bram.us — View Transitions: use the new attr() or match-element for the view-transition-name?

interaction.mouse: Tune duration and easing, or switch the naming strategy between match-element and JS-assigned names.
interaction.click: Shuffle, sort and filter the deck, add or drop rail rows, or mutate both collections in one transition.
interaction.touch: Every control is a tap target; the panel stacks above the demos on narrow screens.

drops.title: Column Pages
drops.description: column-wrap and column-height turn multicol into a magazine spread, and ::column makes each column a snap page.
drops.concept: For twenty years multi-column layout could only make a page taller. Wrapped columns cap each column at column-height and flow into rows, row-rule decorates the horizontal gaps the way column-rule always did the vertical ones, and ::column finally addresses the boxes the fragmenter generated — accepting exactly the properties that cannot disturb layout, which is how a long article becomes a set of scroll-snapped pages with generated markers.
drops.source: Rachel Andrew — Multiple-column layout, rows, rules, and floats

interaction.mouse: Drag column width, height and both gaps; switch the rule style to restyle every gap at once.
interaction.click: Click the page markers under the second demo to jump between column pages.
interaction.touch: Swipe the column pager sideways — each column is its own snap target.

drops.title: Fill the Box
drops.description: text-fit sizes type to the text and the container, where clamp() only ever knew the container.
drops.concept: Fluid type with clamp() scales with the box and ignores the string, so a short headline sits small and a long one overflows. text-fit puts the glyphs in the maths: grow scales up until the line touches the edges, shrink only ever scales down to kill an overflow, per-line fits each line independently, and max-font-size caps the whole thing. The page renders the same headline both ways so the difference is impossible to miss.
drops.source: Roman Komarov — Fit-to-Width status update: prototype and issues

interaction.mouse: Drag container width and base size; retype the headline in the panel and watch both lines re-fit.
interaction.click: Switch the max-font-size ceiling to stop the capped headline climbing.
interaction.touch: Rotate or resize — every fit recomputes, natively or through the measure-and-scale shim.

drops.title: Scrollspy, Unspied
drops.description: scroll-target-group keeps your own anchor markup and lets the browser decide which link is :target-current.
drops.concept: Every docs site ships the same hundred lines: an IntersectionObserver, a guessed threshold, and a class you toggle. scroll-target-group hands that to the engine — mark the nav, keep ordinary anchors, and whichever link points at the thing on screen matches :target-current. Because the markers stay real links they keep their roles, focus rings and hrefs, which the pseudo-element carousel variant cannot offer.

interaction.mouse: Scroll the reader, the filmstrip and the pane stack; drag scroll-margin to change what counts as current.
interaction.click: Click any marker to scroll its own container — the highlight follows without a scroll handler.
interaction.touch: Swipe the filmstrip and flick the pane stack; chips and dots track the gesture.

drops.title: Stylesheet Functions
drops.description: Buttons, cards and a tone ramp built from four @function definitions with typed parameters and defaults.
drops.concept: @function defines real CSS functions — parameters with defaults, a body that can declare its own local custom properties, and a result descriptor. A design system stops being a wall of custom properties and becomes call sites like --tone(var(--hue), 0.78) and --elevation(3). Hover states just pass a different argument, and the panel here drives the arguments live so every call site re-resolves at once.
drops.source: Dan Holloran — CSS @function: reusable logic comes native to the browser

interaction.mouse: Drive the function arguments — hue, elevation level, corner radius and the fluid type range.
interaction.click: Press and hover the buttons; their states pass different values into --elevation().
interaction.touch: Sliders stack above the components on mobile so every variant stays in view.
